chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Dawud, from Ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to Al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, I have dependents and a debt upon me, and my situation has become severe. Teach me a supplication; if I supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with it, Allah will provide for me.'
He said: 'O servant of Allah, perform ablution and perfect your ablution, then pray two rak'ahs, completing the bowing and prostration in them.'
Then say: 'O Magnificent, O Generous, O One, O Generous, I turn to You through Muhammad, Your Prophet, the Prophet of Mercy.'
O Muhammad, O Messenger of Allah, I turn to Allah through You, who is your Lord and the Lord of all things, that You send blessings upon Muhammad and upon his Household.
And I ask You for a breath from Your breaths, a slight opening, and abundant provision, by which I may gather my scattered affairs, pay off my debt, and seek assistance with it for my dependents.'

key_terms.أَتَوَجَّهُ: I turn/face (towards God through an intermediary)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for financial relief and paying off debt according to Imam Al-Rida?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* under the chapter of the 'Prayer of the Needy' (Salat al-Mudtir), this hadith highlights the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt in alleviating worldly distress. The Imam prescribes a specific two-rak'ah prayer followed by a concise dua that links spiritual devotion to material relief, emphasizing the concept of 'nafhat' (divine breath/grace) as a means to settle debts and support dependents.
